transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. I’ve come in because I’ve been having some very unsettling thoughts lately, specifically that people are constantly monitoring my movements. It feels like everyday occurrences and even random comments I hear are actually directed specifically at me, and I can't seem to shake the feeling that something is going on.
Besides these thoughts, have you experienced any periods where your mood was significantly higher or lower than usual, or where your energy levels and sleep patterns changed drastically?
No, I haven't really noticed any significant changes in my mood, energy, or sleep patterns. I feel like those things have stayed pretty much the same as they always are.
Beyond these thoughts about being monitored, have you ever heard voices that others cannot hear, or seen things that others do not see?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that; my concerns are strictly focused on the monitoring I've been feeling. I don't see or hear anything out of the ordinary.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports a fixed belief of being monitored (ideas of reference and persecution) in the absence of mood episodes (ruling out Bipolar/Schizoaffective) and in the absence of auditory or visual hallucinations (making Schizophrenia less likely than Delusional Disorder, which is characterized by non-bizarre or fixed beliefs without prominent hallucinations).
